reference.name: Chilas (overnight stop on the Chilas–Islamabad road transfer)

sources.quote: is a city in Pakistan-administered territory of Gilgit-Baltistan in the disputed Kashmir region.
It is the headquarters of Diamer District and the divisional capital of Diamer Division.

reference.note: 'Chilas to Islamabad' is a road transfer, not one place; the only placeable stop in it is Chilas town (Diamer District), where the group overnights. Pakistan administers GB de facto.

variants.name: ok
variants.rationale: Resolved same: the card is about Chilas town (locality Chilas, town facts). The alias 'Chilas District' is imprecise (today's district is Diamer) but has a historical basis: Wikipedia Diamer_District says 'During the British Raj, the area was known as Chilas'. So the card is not a blend of two entities.

variants.name: ok
variants.rationale: Chilas town in Gilgit-Baltistan; locality left empty; correctly notes the label is a transfer.

sources.quote: It is the headquarters of Diamer District and the divisional capital of Diamer Division.
Chilas is located on the left bank of Indus River.

facts.rationale: Town on the Indus, HQ of Diamer District.

sources.quote: is a city in Pakistan-administered territory of Gilgit-Baltistan in the disputed Kashmir region.
It borders Azad Kashmir to the south, the province of Khyber Pakhtunkhwa to the west

facts.rationale: GB borders Azad (Pakistan-administered) Kashmir and Khyber Pakhtunkhwa.

sources.quote: More than 50,000 Buddhist petroglyphs and inscriptions line the Karakoram Highway in Gilgit-Baltistan, Pakistan.
The carvings were left by various invaders, traders and pilgrims who passed along the trade route, as well as by locals.

facts.rationale: More than 50,000 petroglyphs along the KKH from prehistoric to Buddhist era left by traders/pilgrims; 'one of the largest in the world' is emphatic but consistent.

sources.quote: The earliest date back to between 5000 and 1000 BC, showing single animals, triangular men and hunting scenes
More than 50,000 Buddhist petroglyphs and inscriptions line the Karakoram Highway in Gilgit-Baltistan, Pakistan.

facts.rationale: Prehistoric animals/hunting scenes and Buddhist carvings near Chilas.

sources.quote: It can be reached by the Karakoram Highway and also through the Kaghan Valley via the Babusar Pass.
The route of the KKH traces one of the many paths of the ancient Silk Road.

facts.rationale: Chilas is on the KKH, which links Pakistan and China and traces a Silk Road path.

sources.quote: Lying immediately southeast of the northernmost bend of the Indus River in the Gilgit-Baltistan region of Pakistan-administered Kashmir
The mountain is known locally by its Shina name Diamer or Deo Mir

facts.rationale: Both agree contradicted/false (Diamer is Nanga Parbat's Shina name glossed 'mountain of God', and the peak lies south-east of Chilas, not north). Numeric resolved true: the fact makes an ordinal rank claim ('world's ninth-highest peak'), which Wikipedia confirms ('is the ninth-highest mountain on Earth'), so it is a numeric fact even though the number is not the error.
Arid Indus valley is plausible, but no reliable source found naming the flanking slopes as Karakoram and Hindu Kush foothills (Nanga Parbat Himalaya lies south).

sources.quote: Chilas is located on the left bank of Indus River.
Elevation 1,265 m

facts.rationale: Left bank of the westward-flowing Indus = south bank; 1,265 m within tolerance of ~1,250 m.

sources.quote: It is the headquarters of Diamer District and the divisional capital of Diamer Division.
is a city in Pakistan-administered territory of Gilgit-Baltistan in the disputed Kashmir region.

facts.rationale: Town and HQ of Diamer District in Gilgit-Baltistan.

The route of the KKH traces one of the many paths of the ancient Silk Road.

facts.rationale: Traders and pilgrims passed along the trade route; Buddhist petroglyphs show Silk Road-era contacts.
